candidates.term: The Artisan inside the Hour Gate
candidates.defline: The Artisan lives inside your Hour Gate: your later life settles into good food, deep sleep and people who keep coming back.
candidates.reading: In later life you get to enjoy the comfort you have worked for, and your home fills with younger people and long friendships. Because care has always meant a good meal and a warm bed to you, you keep feeding whoever comes, whether they are children or younger relatives or someone you train. Ease is both the reward of those years and their one risk, and you stay well for as long as your days keep a rhythm.
candidates.teaser: Ease deepens as you age: the root of your late years is comfort earned, kept, and shared. Expect a good table, good sleep, and company that stays.

domain_readings.Family: Your late family gathers by scent: whoever you feed becomes kin, and the kitchen stays the family’s true address. Chosen family counts fully here. Keep hosting past the point that seems sensible. The people you feed become the people who tend you, at astonishing exchange rates.
domain_readings.Health: Ease deepens into your bones with age: sleep improves, appetite steadies, comfort finally guiltless. Your late health asks mostly for rhythm and company. Eat with people whenever you can manage it. Solitary meals age you faster than birthdays do.

candidates.life_chapter: Your late chapter roots in earned comfort: the last decades keep a good table, deep sleep, and company that stays. The blessing is real and it is maintained, by hosting, by rhythm, by refusing to hurry. Expect old age to suit you unusually well. It was built for you.
candidates.relations: The table’s regulars are this seat’s people: children, old friends, the neighbor who somehow always arrives at dinnertime. They are your late-life infrastructure wearing napkins. Keep the guest list warm and the door unlocked. This root feeds on footsteps.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the comfort waits unclaimed: ease deferred as if unearned. Take the nap, book the trip, set the nice table on a Tuesday.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, comfort settles too deep: the couch winning quiet years. Keep one standing engagement that requires shoes.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, ease becomes sediment: cozy, sweet, and slowly sinking.
candidates.health_line: Your late constitution runs on warmth and routine: regular meals, gentle movement, people nearby. Loneliness is the only illness to actually fear.

Family.headline: Your later family is the people at your table.
Family.recognition: You treat anyone who eats at your home often enough as family, and a friend who comes every week matters to you as much as a cousin. Because feeding people is how you show care, you keep inviting people long after others have stopped hosting. Your house stays busy because of it, and you would feel lost in a home that no one visits.
Family.lived: Your home has filled with the people after you since your late forties, and with friends who come for the food. You have hosted more in this stretch than in any earlier decade, and you have started to be fed by the people you once fed.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you gather at your table more each year. The care you have given starts to come back to you in these years, and you are looked after by those you once fed.

Health.headline: Your body grows easier to live in each decade.
Health.recognition: You look after your body through regular meals, gentle movement and people nearby, and it answers you well. Since rest comes easily to you, a good week of it stretches into a slow month before you notice. Your health depends more on company than on effort, and you feel the difference within days when you eat alone.
Health.lived: Your sleep has deepened since your late forties and your appetite has steadied, and you have enjoyed your food more than ever. Your energy has dipped in the stretches when you were on your own too much, and it has come back each time the house filled up again.
Health.ahead: Your body settles into an easy routine from your late forties, with good sleep and steady appetite and company at meals. These years suit your body unusually well, and you stay strong in them while there are people around you.
